lastExecutionStatus.doc: The status of the most recent execution.

scheduleExpression.doc: The cron expression that defines when the scheduled query runs.

timezone.doc: The timezone used for evaluating the schedule expression.

destinationConfiguration.doc: Configuration for where query results are delivered.

creationTime.doc: The timestamp when the scheduled query was created.

lastUpdatedTime.doc: The timestamp when the scheduled query was last updated.

ScheduledQuerySummary.doc: Summary information about a scheduled query, including basic configuration and execution status.

logStreamName.doc: The name of the log stream.

searchedCompletely.doc: Indicates whether all the events in this log stream were searched.

SearchedLogStream.doc: Represents the search status of a log stream.

SessionStreamingException.doc: This exception is returned if an unknown error occurs during a Live Tail session.

SessionTimeoutException.doc: This exception is returned in a Live Tail stream when the Live Tail session times out. Live Tail sessions time out after three hours.

entries.doc: An array of SplitStringEntry objects, where each object contains the information about one field to split.

SplitString.doc: Use this processor to split a field into an array of strings using a delimiting character. For more information about this processor including examples, see splitString in the CloudWatch Logs User Guide.

source.doc: The key of the field to split.

delimiter.doc: The separator characters to split the string entry on.

SplitStringEntry.doc: This object defines one log field that will be split with the splitString processor.

logGroupIdentifiers.doc: An array where each item in the array is a log group to include in the Live Tail session. Specify each log group by its ARN. If you specify an ARN, the ARN can't end with an asterisk (*). You can include up to 10 log groups.

logStreamNames.doc: If you specify this parameter, then only log events in the log streams that you specify here are included in the Live Tail session. If you specify this field, you can't also specify the logStreamNamePrefixes field. You can specify this parameter only if you specify only one log group in logGroupIdentifiers.

logStreamNamePrefixes.doc: If you specify this parameter, then only log events in the log streams that have names that start with the prefixes that you specify here are included in the Live Tail session. If you specify this field, you can't also specify the logStreamNames field. You can specify this parameter only if you specify only one log group in logGroupIdentifiers.

logEventFilterPattern.doc: An optional pattern to use to filter the results to include only log events that match the pattern. For example, a filter pattern of error 404 causes only log events that include both error and 404 to be included in the Live Tail stream. Regular expression filter patterns are supported. For more information about filter pattern syntax, see Filter and Pattern Syntax.

responseStream.doc: An object that includes the stream returned by your request. It can include both log events and exceptions.

sessionStart.doc: This object contains information about this Live Tail session, including the log groups included and the log stream filters, if any.

sessionUpdate.doc: This object contains the log events and session metadata.

SessionTimeoutException.doc: This exception is returned in the stream when the Live Tail session times out. Live Tail sessions time out after three hours.

SessionStreamingException.doc: This exception is returned if an unknown error occurs.

StartLiveTailResponseStream.doc: This object includes the stream returned by your StartLiveTail request.

queryLanguage.doc: Specify the query language to use for this query. The options are Logs Insights QL, OpenSearch PPL, and OpenSearch SQL. For more information about the query languages that CloudWatch Logs supports, see Supported query languages.

logGroupName.doc: The log group on which to perform the query. A StartQuery operation must include exactly one of the following parameters: logGroupName, logGroupNames, or logGroupIdentifiers. The exception is queries using the OpenSearch Service SQL query language, where you specify the log group names inside the querystring instead of here.

logGroupNames.doc: The list of log groups to be queried. You can include up to 50 log groups. A StartQuery operation must include exactly one of the following parameters: logGroupName, logGroupNames, or logGroupIdentifiers. The exception is queries using the OpenSearch Service SQL query language, where you specify the log group names inside the querystring instead of here.

logGroupIdentifiers.doc: The list of log groups to query. You can include up to 50 log groups. You can specify them by the log group name or ARN. If a log group that you're querying is in a source account and you're using a monitoring account, you must specify the ARN of the log group here. The query definition must also be defined in the monitoring account. If you specify an ARN, use the format…

startTime.doc: The beginning of the time range to query. The range is inclusive, so the specified start time is included in the query. Specified as epoch time, the number of seconds since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC.

endTime.doc: The end of the time range to query. The range is inclusive, so the specified end time is included in the query. Specified as epoch time, the number of seconds since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC.

queryString.doc: The query string to use. For more information, see CloudWatch Logs Insights Query Syntax.

limit.doc: The maximum number of log events to return from the query. The maximum limit is 100,000. The maximum events returned in a single GetQueryResults API call is 10,000 log events per request. You can retrieve up to 100,000 log event results from a query by paginating with the nextToken. 100,000 limit is only supported for Logs Insights QL and is currently not supported for PPL and SQL query languages.

queryId.doc: The unique ID of the query.
The ID number of the query to stop. To find this ID number, use DescribeQueries.

success.doc: This is true if the query was stopped by the StopQuery operation.

filterName.doc: The name of the subscription filter.

logGroupName.doc: The name of the log group.

destinationArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the destination.

applyOnTransformedLogs.doc: This parameter is valid only for log groups that have an active log transformer. For more information about log transformers, see PutTransformer. If this value is true, the subscription filter is applied on the transformed version of the log events instead of the original ingested log events.

creationTime.doc: The creation time of the subscription filter, expressed as the number of milliseconds after Jan 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC.

fieldSelectionCriteria.doc: The filter expression that specifies which log events are processed by this subscription filter based on system fields. Returns the fieldSelectionCriteria value if it was specified when the subscription filter was created.

emitSystemFields.doc: The list of system fields that are included in the log events sent to the subscription destination. Returns the emitSystemFields value if it was specified when the subscription filter was created.

entries.doc: An array of objects, where each object contains the information about one key to match and replace.

SubstituteString.doc: This processor matches a key’s value against a regular expression and replaces all matches with a replacement string. For more information about this processor including examples, see substituteString in the CloudWatch Logs User Guide.

from.doc: The regular expression string to be replaced. Special regex characters such as [ and ] must be escaped using \\ when using double quotes and with \ when using single quotes. For more information, see Class Pattern on the Oracle web site.

to.doc: The string to be substituted for each match of from

SubstituteStringEntry.doc: This object defines one log field key that will be replaced using the substituteString processor.

value.doc: Specifies the number of seconds, minutes or hours to suppress this anomaly. There is no maximum.

suppressionUnit.doc: Specifies whether the value of value is in seconds, minutes, or hours.

SuppressionPeriod.doc: If you are suppressing an anomaly temporariliy, this structure defines how long the suppression period is to be.

logGroupArn.doc: The ARN of the log group associated with this syslog configuration.

sourceType.doc: The source type for the syslog configuration.

vpcEndpointId.doc: The ID of the VPC endpoint used for syslog ingestion.

createdAt.doc: The time when the syslog configuration was created, expressed as the number of milliseconds after Jan 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC.

SyslogConfiguration.doc: Contains information about a syslog configuration associated with a log group.

key.doc: The tag key to filter on.

values.doc: An optional list of tag values to filter on. If you specify a filter that contains more than one value for a key, the response returns log groups that match any of the specified values for that key. If you don't specify values, the response returns all log groups that are tagged with that key, with any or no value. Use * for wildcard matching. For example, prod* matches values that start with…

TagFilter.doc: A tag filter that specifies a tag key and optional tag values for filtering log groups by tags.

logGroupName.doc: The name of the log group.

tags.doc: The key-value pairs to use for the tags.

resourceArn.doc: The ARN of the resource that you're adding tags to. The ARN format of a log group is arn:aws:logs:Region:account-id:log-group:log-group-name The ARN format of a destination is arn:aws:logs:Region:account-id:destination:destination-name For more information about ARN format, see CloudWatch Logs resources and operations.

tags.doc: The list of key-value pairs to associate with the resource.

logEventMessages.doc: The log event messages to test.

transformerConfig.doc: This structure contains the configuration of this log transformer that you want to test. A log transformer is an array of processors, where each processor applies one type of transformation to the log events that are ingested.

logEventMessages.doc: An array of the raw log events that you want to use to test this transformer.

transformedLogs.doc: An array where each member of the array includes both the original version and the transformed version of one of the log events that you input.

eventMessage.doc: The original log event message before it was transformed.

transformedEventMessage.doc: The log event message after being transformed.

TransformedLogRecord.doc: This structure contains information for one log event that has been processed by a log transformer.

queryId.doc: The unique identifier for this query execution.

executionStatus.doc: The execution status of the scheduled query run.

triggeredTimestamp.doc: The timestamp when the scheduled query execution was triggered.

errorMessage.doc: Error message if the query execution failed.

destinations.doc: Information about destination processing for this query execution.

TriggerHistoryRecord.doc: A record of a scheduled query execution, including execution status, timestamp, and destination processing results.

withKeys.doc: The array containing the keys of the fields to trim.

TrimString.doc: Use this processor to remove leading and trailing whitespace. For more information about this processor including examples, see trimString in the CloudWatch Logs User Guide.

entries.doc: An array of TypeConverterEntry objects, where each object contains the information about one field to change the type of.

TypeConverter.doc: Use this processor to convert a value type associated with the specified key to the specified type. It's a casting processor that changes the types of the specified fields. Values can be converted into one of the following datatypes: integer, double, string and boolean. For more information about this processor including examples, see trimString in the CloudWatch Logs User Guide.

key.doc: The key with the value that is to be converted to a different type.

type.doc: The type to convert the field value to. Valid values are integer, double, string and boolean.

TypeConverterEntry.doc: This object defines one value type that will be converted using the typeConverter processor.

logGroupName.doc: The name of the log group.

tags.doc: The tag keys. The corresponding tags are removed from the log group.

resourceArn.doc: The ARN of the CloudWatch Logs resource that you're removing tags from. The ARN format of a log group is arn:aws:logs:Region:account-id:log-group:log-group-name The ARN format of a destination is arn:aws:logs:Region:account-id:destination:destination-name For more information about ARN format, see CloudWatch Logs resources and operations.

tagKeys.doc: The list of tag keys to remove from the resource.

anomalyId.doc: If you are suppressing or unsuppressing an anomaly, specify its unique ID here. You can find anomaly IDs by using the ListAnomalies operation.

patternId.doc: If you are suppressing or unsuppressing an pattern, specify its unique ID here. You can find pattern IDs by using the ListAnomalies operation.

anomalyDetectorArn.doc: The ARN of the anomaly detector that this operation is to act on.

suppressionType.doc: Use this to specify whether the suppression to be temporary or infinite. If you specify LIMITED, you must also specify a suppressionPeriod. If you specify INFINITE, any value for suppressionPeriod is ignored.

suppressionPeriod.doc: If you are temporarily suppressing an anomaly or pattern, use this structure to specify how long the suppression is to last.

baseline.doc: Set this to true to prevent CloudWatch Logs from displaying this behavior as an anomaly in the future. The behavior is then treated as baseline behavior. However, if similar but more severe occurrences of this behavior occur in the future, those will still be reported as anomalies. The default is false

id.doc: The ID of the delivery to be updated by this request.

recordFields.doc: The list of record fields to be delivered to the destination, in order. If the delivery's log source has mandatory fields, they must be included in this list.

fieldDelimiter.doc: The field delimiter to use between record fields when the final output format of a delivery is in Plain, W3C, or Raw format.

s3DeliveryConfiguration.doc: This structure contains parameters that are valid only when the delivery's delivery destination is an S3 bucket.

anomalyDetectorArn.doc: The ARN of the anomaly detector that you want to update.

evaluationFrequency.doc: Specifies how often the anomaly detector runs and look for anomalies. Set this value according to the frequency that the log group receives new logs. For example, if the log group receives new log events every 10 minutes, then setting evaluationFrequency to FIFTEEN_MIN might be appropriate.

anomalyVisibilityTime.doc: The number of days to use as the life cycle of anomalies. After this time, anomalies are automatically baselined and the anomaly detector model will treat new occurrences of similar event as normal. Therefore, if you do not correct the cause of an anomaly during this time, it will be considered normal going forward and will not be detected.

enabled.doc: Use this parameter to pause or restart the anomaly detector.

lookupTableArn.doc: The ARN of the lookup table to update.

description.doc: An updated description of the lookup table.

tableBody.doc: The new CSV content to replace the existing data. The first row must be a header row with column names. The content must use UTF-8 encoding and not exceed 10 MB. You must specify either tableBody or queryId, but not both.

queryId.doc: The ID of a completed or cancelled CloudWatch Logs query whose results replace the lookup table content. A cancelled query replaces the content with the partial results that were available when the query was stopped. You must specify either tableBody or queryId, but not both.

kmsKeyId.doc: The ARN of the KMS key to use to encrypt the lookup table data. You can use this parameter to add, update, or remove the KMS key. To remove the KMS key and use an Amazon Web Services-owned key instead, specify an empty string.

lookupTableArn.doc: The ARN of the lookup table that was updated.

lastUpdatedTime.doc: The time when the lookup table was last updated, expressed as the number of milliseconds after Jan 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC.

identifier.doc: The ARN or name of the scheduled query to update.

description.doc: An updated description for the scheduled query.

queryLanguage.doc: The updated query language for the scheduled query.

queryString.doc: The updated query string to execute.

logGroupIdentifiers.doc: The updated array of log group names or ARNs to query.

scheduleExpression.doc: The updated cron expression that defines when the scheduled query runs.

timezone.doc: The updated timezone for evaluating the schedule expression.

startTimeOffset.doc: The updated time offset in seconds that defines the lookback period for the query.

endTimeOffset.doc: The updated time offset in seconds that defines the end of the lookback period for the query.

destinationConfiguration.doc: The updated configuration for where to deliver query results.

scheduleStartTime.doc: The updated start time for the scheduled query in Unix epoch format.

scheduleEndTime.doc: The updated end time for the scheduled query in Unix epoch format.

executionRoleArn.doc: The updated ARN of the IAM role that grants permissions to execute the query and deliver results.

state.doc: The updated state of the scheduled query.

scheduledQueryArn.doc: The ARN of the updated scheduled query.

name.doc: The name of the updated scheduled query.

description.doc: The description of the updated scheduled query.

queryLanguage.doc: The query language of the updated scheduled query.

queryString.doc: The query string of the updated scheduled query.

logGroupIdentifiers.doc: The log groups queried by the updated scheduled query.

scheduleExpression.doc: The cron expression of the updated scheduled query.

timezone.doc: The timezone of the updated scheduled query.

startTimeOffset.doc: The time offset of the updated scheduled query.

endTimeOffset.doc: The end time offset in seconds of the updated scheduled query.

destinationConfiguration.doc: The destination configuration of the updated scheduled query.

state.doc: The state of the updated scheduled query.

scheduleType.doc: The schedule type of the updated scheduled query.

lastTriggeredTime.doc: The timestamp when the updated scheduled query was last executed.

lastExecutionStatus.doc: The status of the most recent execution of the updated scheduled query.

scheduleStartTime.doc: The start time of the updated scheduled query.

scheduleEndTime.doc: The end time of the updated scheduled query.

executionRoleArn.doc: The execution role ARN of the updated scheduled query.

creationTime.doc: The timestamp when the scheduled query was originally created.

lastUpdatedTime.doc: The timestamp when the scheduled query was last updated.

withKeys.doc: The array of containing the keys of the field to convert to uppercase.

UpperCaseString.doc: This processor converts a string field to uppercase. For more information about this processor including examples, see upperCaseString in the CloudWatch Logs User Guide.
